S1.text: A humanoid robot, for under twenty-five hundred dollars.

S1.2.text: It launched in mid-October, and every headline led with the price.

S2.2.text: And behind it is a bigger story: the firms that count these robots can't agree on how many there are, or what they're for.

S3.text: It's called FF Nova, from Faraday Future, the electric car company, and its robotics sister company.

S3.2.text: It has twenty joints. It walks, it waves, and it gets back up after being knocked over.

S3.3.text: It runs ROS 2, a widely used robotics framework.

S3.4.text: The first hundred units are invitation only, for developers and schools.

S3.5.text: And a kids' version, Nova Mini, costs two hundred and ninety-nine dollars.

S4.2.text: It's forty-nine point seven centimeters tall. About knee high.

S4.3.text: And it weighs two point eight kilos. Less than a gallon of milk.

S5.text: That doesn't make it a gimmick.

S5.2.text: A small robot that can fall over and get back up is a good way to learn robotics.

S5.3.text: It's priced for classrooms and developers. Not for your kitchen.

S6.2.text: How many humanoid robots shipped in the first half of 2026?

S6.3.text: Smart Analytics Global says about nineteen thousand.

S6.4.text: Counterpoint Research says over twenty-two thousand.

S6.6.text: Same six months. Almost six thousand robots apart.

S7.text: They don't agree on what the robots are doing, either.

S7.2.text: IDC says sixty-nine percent went to research, education, shows, and government data collection.

S7.3.text: Smart Analytics Global says over seventy percent went to industrial and commercial work.

S8.text: Even China's share depends on the question.

S8.2.text: About seventy-eight percent were bought in China.

S8.3.text: Over ninety-five percent were built by Chinese companies.

S9.text: So, will a humanoid do your chores?

S9.2.text: Not the ones you can buy today.

S9.3.text: The robots already working in homes are narrow: vacuums, lawn mowers, garden robots like FarmBot.

S9.4.text: Each one does a single job, on a schedule.

S10.text: What to watch next: whether Nova ships beyond the first hundred.

S10.2.text: And the full-year counts. The forecasts run from over fifty thousand to about sixty thousand.

S11.2.text: Getting useful is the next test.
